affiliations.occupation: Occupations in manufacture of tobacco products
affiliations.date_precision: The identifier-matched Enlisted Reserve Corps statistical card dated 9 December 1942 carries civilian-occupation value 412; the official table defines 4-12 as the skilled level of a broad tobacco-manufacturing group.
affiliations.research_notes: The broad category does not establish a specific task, tobacco product, employer, factory, city, paid relationship, work dates or Army-to-OSS sequence.

affiliations.date_precision: McIntosh Laboratory says Corderman joined OSS in 1942 at age sixteen and remained in high school while continuing OSS work. His exact-identifier Army row dated 11 January 1944 independently carries student code 992.
affiliations.research_notes: The institution is not named. Student status is not employment, and the 1944 Army code corroborates status at Army entry rather than supplying the 1942 OSS date.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Georges Cordeau is a high-confidence match to the French intelligence-network agent whose official SHD file is GR 28 P 4 175/187.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official French finding aid lists Georges Cordeau in an intelligence-network agents series; a source-referenced mission register connects that name and file to Proust/OSS/Midiron wireless work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon exact name, the index's printed French note and S/Lt rank, the official SHD agent file, and the independent OSS-linked mission register support a high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The SHD file's documents begin in 1943 and the mission register describes 1944-1945 activity; neither establishes Cordeau's immediate pre-OSS affiliation or civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: No birth date appears in the index, so the identity is not marked confirmed. The printed S/Lt abbreviation is preserved without expanding it into an unqualified commissioned rank.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Sidney A Corderman has a confirmed Army-record identity and is the Sidney Corderman whom McIntosh Laboratory documents as joining OSS in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact private identifier selects a 1944 Army row with birth-year code 1925; McIntosh reports that Corderman joined OSS in 1942 at sixteen and was drafted at eighteen.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact private identifier and exact full name confirm the Army identity; the matching age chronology, uncommon name and direct OSS account bridge the institutional biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: McIntosh dates civilian OSS entry to 1942 and Army continuation after the draft; the Army record independently dates entry to 11 January 1944.
claims.match_notes: The adjacent unnumbered Sidney Corderman source row remains a separate possible duplicate. No facts are transferred to it before Box 144 review.

claims.claim_text: Sidney A Corderman was a high-school student when he joined OSS in 1942; the school is not identified and student status is not employment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: finish high school and continue working at the OSS
claims.evidence_paraphrase: McIntosh reports that Corderman joined OSS at sixteen and continued high school while working there; the exact-identifier 1944 Army row also carries the official student code.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact-identifier Army row, matching 1925 birth-year code, uncommon name and McIntosh OSS chronology establish the same person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional account directly places high-school status at and around his 1942 OSS entry; the 1944 Army code independently corroborates continuing student status.
claims.match_notes: No school is inferred, and the relationship is modeled as student rather than employment. The Army code does not by itself prove the 1942 sequence.

The identifier has no literal fixed-width Army match, and reviewed official, OSS, CIA, newspaper, obituary, institutional and archival searches do not establish a unique identity.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 144 to identify Pauline Corbitt's numbering system, personnel status, full identity, pre-OSS affiliation and employer.
